intro: Long before microscopes and hospitals, people still got sick and hurt. Healers in Egypt, Greece, Rome, China and India worked hard to help them. They watched patients, tried treatments and wrote down what they learned on papyrus, silk, bamboo and palm leaves. Some of those writings survive today.

In this unit you will read about Egyptian medical rolls, Hippocrates and the four humors, Galen and Roman aqueducts, the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic and the great books of Ayurveda. You will see which ideas lasted, which were replaced, and how science tests old ideas.

By the end, you will be able to compare how ancient traditions explained health. You will be able to tell a tradition's ideas apart from what scientific evidence shows. And you will know why it helps to tell a doctor or pharmacist about any remedy you use.
bigQuestion: How did ancient peoples explain and treat illness, and how do we decide which of their ideas still help us today?

timeline.t: The Edwin Smith Papyrus records 48 injury cases in Egypt
The Ebers Papyrus collects about 700 Egyptian remedies
Hippocratic writers in Greece teach natural causes and the four humors
Rome builds the Aqua Appia, its first aqueduct
The Huangdi Neijing takes shape in China, around this time
The Charaka and Sushruta collections take shape in India over these centuries
Galen of Pergamon works in Rome and writes his many books
Andreas Vesalius corrects many of Galen's anatomy mistakes
Rudolf Virchow argues that disease begins in cells
Tu Youyou wins a Nobel Prize for artemisinin, a malaria medicine

words.d: a paper-like writing material made in ancient Egypt from a river reed
a prediction about how an illness or injury will turn out
the four body fluids in the old Greek theory: blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile
the study of the structure and parts of the body
carefully cutting open a body to study its parts
a channel or bridge that carries water from a distant source to a city
work that protects the health of a whole community, such as clean water
in Traditional Chinese Medicine, the vital energy said to flow through the body
in TCM, channels through which qi is said to flow
in Ayurveda, the three basic forces said to shape the body: vata, pitta and kapha
treating the body by cutting, repairing or removing parts
facts or observations that show whether an idea is true

test.q: What is the Edwin Smith Papyrus best known for?
test.why: The Edwin Smith Papyrus describes 48 injury cases from the head downward.

test.q: Which idea did Hippocratic writers stress?
choices: Illness is a punishment from gods
Surgery must be practiced on melons
test.why: Hippocratic writers taught that illness has natural causes.

test.q: Which tradition taught the four humors?
test.why: The four humors came from Greek medicine and were later used by Galen.

test.q: Why did Galen's anatomy contain errors?
test.why: Galen dissected animals, whose bodies differ from human bodies in some ways.

test.q: What did Roman aqueducts do for health?
choices: Brought clean water to many people
test.why: Aqueducts brought clean water to fountains, homes and baths, an early form of public health.

test.q: Which book is a founding text of TCM?
choices: On the Fabric of the Human Body
test.why: The Huangdi Neijing is the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic, a founding TCM text.

test.q: In TCM, which pair of forces must stay in balance?
test.why: TCM teaches that health needs a balance of yin and yang.

test.q: Which Ayurvedic book is mainly about surgery?
test.why: The Sushruta Samhita is one of the earliest detailed books on surgery.

test.q: Which three doshas does Ayurveda teach?
test.why: Ayurveda's three doshas are vata, pitta and kapha.

test.q: Which surgery from the Sushruta Samhita still inspires surgeons today?
choices: Rebuilding a nose with a skin flap
Couching a cataract with a needle
test.why: Skin flaps that stay attached to their blood supply are still used in reconstructive surgery.

test.q: What finally replaced the humors theory?
test.why: Virchow's cell work and Pasteur and Koch's germ work did not fit the humors.

test.q: What does scientific evidence say about acupuncture?
choices: Meridians have been seen in dissection
It helps some people with certain pain, but why is debated
test.why: Some studies show help for certain pain, but fake needling often helps too.

test.q: How did an old Chinese text help modern medicine?
choices: It led Tu Youyou to artemisinin for malaria
test.why: Tu Youyou's team found artemisinin after reading an old text about sweet wormwood.

test.q: What did a 2008 study find about some Ayurvedic products sold online?
choices: About one in five contained heavy metals
They were all made in Rome
test.why: Saper's 2008 study found about one in five contained lead, mercury or arsenic.

test.q: Which habit is shared by Egyptian healers, Hippocrates, Sushruta and modern doctors?
test.why: Each valued close observation of patients and careful practice.

write.prompt: Pick one ancient tradition from this unit: Egyptian, Greek and Roman, Chinese or Indian. Which of its ideas or practices still helps people today, and which has been replaced? Use two or three facts or sources from the unit to support your claim.
tips: Name your sources, such as the Edwin Smith Papyrus or the Sushruta Samhita.
Describe the tradition respectfully and in its own terms.
Say plainly what scientific evidence shows.
Use unit words like evidence, prognosis or public health.
End by explaining how you decided.
